text:
incidents-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: GPU hotpath (us-west-2) pool 'hot-64' entering sustained saturation. queue length +320% over baseline, 429s rising. Auto-scale attempts failing with 'scale_limit_reached'. Paging SRE oncall.

kevin-oncall: saw the page, jumping on. checking autoscaler logs now. anyone know if we recently changed tokenbucket for tier=gold?

maya: not that I'm aware of. looking at metrics -> tokenbucket depletion on hot-64, token refill rate looks normal but consumed very quickly. lots of small short requests + async bursts.

jon-eng: we rolled a policy patch yesterday that tightened per-route token limits for the chat-hotpath to curb abuse. could be interaction under surge. linking PR: https://git.internal/r/redwood/infra/pulls/1422

pradeep: timeline: 16:42 UTC spike started, autoscaler attempted 3 scale outs, last attempt failed with "gpu_quota_exhausted" from cloud provider, then local scale rejected due to pool max_instances=24.

kevin-oncall: ok immediate mitigations: 1) relax tokenbucket refill for tier=gold on the hotpath to halve token_cost temporarily; 2) route lower-priority traffic to fallback pool 'warm-64'; 3) emergency canary to a quantized model variant to reduce GPU memory and increase parallelism. who's on it?

maya: doing (1) now. running safe edit against config service: `rbacctl patch tokenbucket --name=gold-hotpath --refill-rate=2000` -> applying.

sre-runbook-bot: runbook step triggered: "tokenbucket-temporary-relax". suggested TTL=30m.

jon-eng: starting route update to move /v1/chat-hotpath low-priority route -> warm-64. patch: ```
PATCH /routes/chat-hotpath
{ "traffic_split": { "hot-64": 0.6, "warm-64": 0.4 } }
```

pradeep: creating a short-lived override for pool max_instances to 32. hitting cloud quota limits but ops team approved emergency bump. request id 0x7b4 -> accepted. autoscaler should retry.

kevin-oncall: after those changes, monitor 429 rate + queue length. set alert to 5min windows. maya pls confirm token refill applied and show counters.

maya: token refills applied. sample counters: `tokens_per_sec (gold-hotpath): before=800 now=2000` ; token_consumed/sec peaked at 28k, now down to ~9k. queue depth decreased from 1200 -> 420 in 6 minutes. 429 rate dropped 68% in first 4 mins.

lisa-cs: Customer impact: CS reports elevated latencies for a handful of enterprise users on us-west-2, some API errors with 429. Team is preparing comms. no escalations to execs yet.

jon-eng: pushing quantized variant rollout to hot-64 for 10% of traffic. command below: ```
POST /deployments/rollout
{ "model_variant": "gptq-13b-8bit", "routes": ["/v1/chat-hotpath"], "percent": 10 }
```

pradeep: autoscaler retried and succeeded scaling hot-64 to 28 instances once quota bump landed. new capacity coming up.

kevin-oncall: good. continue monitoring. next: schedule a controlled throttle change to tokenbucket thresholds — we need to avoid oscillation when refill is high and demand bursts return. we should add a smoothing window.

maya: noted. opening a temporary smoothing rule: `tokenbucket.smoothing_window=30s` to reduce short-term bursts, will revert in 45m.

sre-runbook-bot: post-mitigation checklist: record start_ts=1789012345, mitigation_actions=["relax_tokenbucket","route_shift","pool_quota_bump","quantized_canary"], impact=partial (latency + 429 for subset).

kevin-oncall: handing off to night shift: maya will continue active monitoring for next 30m then hand to oncall-night. if 429s < 1% and queue <200 for 15m, we can start rollback of emergency changes.

maya: taking active. I'll annotate dashboards and create a short incident note. pls tag if anyone sees regression.

lisa-cs: drafting customer note: "We experienced elevated throttling in us-west-2 affecting chat endpoints. We applied temporary rate tuning and failover to reduce errors. We're continuing to monitor and will follow up with root cause." sending to affected customers in 15m if stable.

jon-eng: follow-up action items (post-incident): - revert tokenbucket temporary-relax and implement adaptive refill with smoothing - revisit tier policies to ensure gold routes don't starve hotpool - add guardrails around pool max_instances bump (auto-fallback to alternate regions) - add synthetic load tests emulating mixed short/long requests to validate token costs.

kevin-oncall: thanks team. I'll update PagerDuty handoff and mark incident as mitigated in 15m if metrics hold. :thumbsup:

sre-runbook-bot: incident state -> mitigated_pending_observation. will auto-close if stable for 30m.

maya: last note: logs show a small percentage (~2%) of client retries causing token amplification (retry storm). need to tell client teams to implement jitter/exponential backoff. adding to follow-up.

kevin-oncall: handing off at 1789012420 to night oncall. maya, please DM me any escalation. good work everyone. :tada:
